legend: Thomas has been caught game (again)! Instead of playing on a 2d grid, he is now playing on a multidimensional space that has no regard to fundamental axioms of geometry, more commonly known as a graph. Thomas is on a graph of n$$$n$$$ nodes completely full with an undirected edge between all u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ such that (1≤u<v≤n)$$$(1 \leq u  \lt  v \leq n)$$$. Teacher is trying to catch Thomas and has already blocked off m$$$m$$$ of these edges.
Thomas is trying to run out of the graph before Teacher comes and catches him. Thomas is able to escape from a node if it has degree at most 1$$$1$$$ or there is at most 1$$$1$$$ edge out of it.

As it turns out, Teacher still has not used his secret weapon yet. Teacher has a powerful device that is able to delete 2$$$2$$$ nodes. When a node is deleted, all of the edges that go out of that node are removed from the graph.

Thomas now wants your help to help check if escaping from Teacher's grasp is possible. Thomas will ask you q$$$q$$$ queries, where each query is two integers a$$$a$$$ b$$$b$$$. Thomas wants you to answer the total number of escapable nodes in the graph if Teacher deletes the nodes a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$ with his machine.
input: The first line containers three integers n$$$n$$$ m$$$m$$$ k$$$k$$$ (2≤n≤2⋅105),(1≤q≤2⋅105),(0≤m≤min(n(n−1)2,2⋅105))$$$(2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5), (1 \leq q \leq 2 \cdot 10^5), (0 \leq m \leq \min(\frac{n(n-1)}{2}, 2 \cdot 10^5))$$$. The next m$$$m$$$ lines contain two integers each u$$$u$$$ v$$$v$$$ (1≤u,v≤n,u≠v)$$$(1 \leq u, v \leq n, u \neq v)$$$. It is guaranteed no edge will appear twice in the input. The following q$$$q$$$ lines contain two integers each a$$$a$$$ b$$$b$$$ (1≤a,b≤n,a≠b)$$$(1 \leq a, b \leq n, a \neq b)$$$ denoting a query of Teacher deleting the nodes a$$$a$$$ and b$$$b$$$. All queries are independant, meaning Teacher does not actually delete any nodes, but rather we are considering the case if he hypothetically did.
output: You will output q$$$q$$$ lines, the i$$$i$$$'th line denoting the answer to the i′th$$$i'th$$$ query.
note: In the first query, the escapable nodes are 4$$$4$$$ and 5$$$5$$$.
In the second query, there are no escapable nodes.

legend.ai: Thomas 又被抓到玩游戏了！这次他不再是在二维网格上玩，而是在一个不遵循几何基本公理的多维空间中进行游戏，这种空间更常见的名称是图。Thomas 位于一个有 n$$$n$$$ 个节点的图中，任意满足 (1≤u<v≤n)$$$(1 \leq u  \lt  v \leq n)$$$ 的 u$$$u$$$ 和 v$$$v$$$ 之间都有一条无向边，图中原本完全连通。Teacher 正试图抓住 Thomas，并且已经封锁了其中的 m$$$m$$$ 条边。
Thomas 正试图在 Teacher 赶来抓住他之前逃出图。如果一个节点的度数至多为 1$$$1$$$，或者从该节点连出的边至多有 1$$$1$$$ 条，那么 Thomas 就能从该节点逃脱。
然而，Teacher 还没有使用他的秘密武器。Teacher 有一个强大的设备，可以删除 2$$$2$$$ 个节点。当一个节点被删除时，所有从该节点连出的边都会从图中移除。
现在 Thomas 希望你帮助他判断是否能够逃脱 Teacher 的掌控。Thomas 会提出 q$$$q$$$ 个查询，每个查询包含两个整数 a$$$a$$$ b$$$b$$$。如果 Teacher 使用机器删除节点 a$$$a$$$ 和 b$$$b$$$，Thomas 希望你回答图中可逃脱节点的总数。

input.ai: 第一行包含三个整数 n$$$n$$$、m$$$m$$$、k$$$k$$$ (2≤n≤2⋅105),(1≤q≤2⋅105),(0≤m≤min(n(n−1)2,2⋅105))$$$(2 \leq n \leq 2 \cdot 10^5), (1 \leq q \leq 2 \cdot 10^5), (0 \leq m \leq \min(\frac{n(n-1)}{2}, 2 \cdot 10^5))$$$。接下来的 m$$$m$$$ 行每行包含两个整数 u$$$u$$$ v$$$v$$$ (1≤u,v≤n,u≠v)$$$(1 \leq u, v \leq n, u \neq v)$$$。保证输入中不会有重复出现的边。接下来的 q$$$q$$$ 行每行包含两个整数 a$$$a$$$ b$$$b$$$ (1≤a,b≤n,a≠b)$$$(1 \leq a, b \leq n, a \neq b)$$$，表示 Teacher 删除节点 a$$$a$$$ 和 b$$$b$$$ 的查询。所有查询相互独立，这意味着 Teacher 实际上不会删除任何节点，我们只考虑他假设删除这些节点时的情况。

output.ai: 你需要输出 q$$$q$$$ 行，其中第 i$$$i$$$ 行表示第 i′$$$i'th$$$ 个查询的答案。

note.ai: 在第一个查询中，可逃脱的节点为 4$$$4$$$ 和 5$$$5$$$。
在第二个查询中，没有可逃脱的节点。
